# 1 Clement Chapter 55 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 55 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_055_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 55

**55:1** But that we may bring forward also examples of Gentiles: many kings and rulers, in a time of pestilence, being moved by oracles, delivered themselves over to death, that they might deliver their fellow-citizens through their own blood. Many departed from their own cities that rebellions might be brought to an end.

**55:2** We know many among ourselves who gave themselves over to bondage that they might ransom others. Many sold themselves into slavery and with the price received for themselves they fed others.

**55:3** Many women, being empowered through the grace of God, did many deeds of manly valor.

**55:4** The blessed Judith, when the city was besieged, asked the elders to permit her to go out to the camp of the foreigners.

**55:5** So she delivered herself over to peril and went out from love of country and of the people who were in siege — and the LORD delivered Holofernes into the hands of a woman.

**55:6** No less also the blessed Esther, being perfect in faith, delivered herself over to peril in order to rescue the twelve tribes of Israel who were about to be destroyed. For with fasting and self-abasement she besought the all-seeing Master; and he, beholding the humility of her soul, delivered the people for whose sake she had exposed herself to peril.

---

*EMET renders the Greek of Codex Alexandrinus with maximal literalness.*
